title: Left Atrial Global Longitudinal Strain Predicts Recurrence After Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation is an effective treatment for atrial fibrillation (AF), but postablation recurrence remains common. This study evaluated whether baseline absolute left atrial global longitudinal strain (LAGLS) predicts AF recurrence after catheter ablation.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 272 patients undergoing first-time radiofrequency catheter ablation. Baseline LAGLS was measured using two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography. AF recurrence was assessed during 12 months of follow-up.

RESULTS: AF recurrence occurred in 53 patients (19.5%). In the fully adjusted multivariable model, longer AF duration (OR = 1.151, 95% CI: 1.041-1.273; p = 0.006) and lower absolute LAGLS (OR = 0.755, 95% CI: 0.679-0.839; p < 0.001) were independently associated with recurrence. Absolute LAGLS showed good discrimination, with an AUC of 0.802 (95% CI: 0.749-0.855; p < 0.001). Within this cohort, a LAGLS threshold of 6.06%, derived using the Youden index, was associated with a higher risk of AF recurrence.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower baseline absolute LAGLS and longer AF duration were independently associated with AF recurrence. Preprocedural LAGLS assessment may assist postablation risk stratification and surveillance.

title: Efficiency, Efficacy, and Energy-Specific Safety of Pulsed Field Versus Thermal Ablation in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: Insights From Contemporary Randomized Data (the E3-PFA Collaboration).
summary:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an increasingly adopted, minimally thermal modality for the ablation of atrial fibrillation, but its comparative performance versus contemporary thermal ablation strategies remains incompletely defined. We conducted an aggregate-data meta-analysis of contemporary randomized trials to compare procedural performance, safety, and clinical outcomes of PFA versus cryoballoon ablation and radiofrequency ablation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

METHODS: A systematic search identified 6 contemporary randomized controlled trials enrolling 2015 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. Study-level random-effects meta-analyses were performed to compare procedural performance, peri-procedural safety, and atrial arrhythmia recurrence, with predefined subgroup analyses according to thermal ablation modality.

RESULTS: PFA was associated with significantly shorter procedure time, left atrial dwell time, and total ablation time than thermal ablation (all P<0.001), whereas fluoroscopy time and anesthetic strategy were comparable between groups. PFA was associated with a significantly lower risk of peri-procedural serious adverse events than thermal ablation (risk ratio, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.35-0.96]; P=0.036). Persistent phrenic nerve palsy and pulmonary vein stenosis occurred exclusively after thermal ablation. Overall, PFA was associated with a lower risk of atrial arrhythmia recurrence than pooled thermal ablation (risk ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.75-0.99]; P=0.03). Subgroup analyses demonstrated a significant reduction in recurrence compared with cryoballoon ablation (risk ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.65-0.97]; P=0.03), whereas outcomes were comparable between PFA and contemporary radiofrequency (risk ratio, 0.93 [95% CI, 0.77-1.13]; P=0.48).

CONCLUSIONS: PFA provides greater procedural efficiency, improved peri-procedural safety, and a lower risk of atrial arrhythmia recurrence than pooled thermal ablation in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The efficacy advantage was primarily driven by comparisons with cryoballoon ablation, whereas outcomes were comparable between PFA and contemporary RFA.

title: First-in-Man Use of the Tau20-RETROmapping System to Identify and Guide Ablation of Ectopy-Triggering Ganglionated Plexuses During Sinus Rhythm as Nonpulmonary Vein Drivers of Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary vein (PV) isolation is ineffective in a proportion of patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). The Tau20-RETROmapping system was developed to help identify non-PV drivers of AF. We tested the feasibility of using the system to guide ablation of non-PV drivers during sinus rhythm.

METHODS: This was a prospective feasibility study of only non-PV ablation in patients with symptomatic AF. The Tau20-RETROmapping system was used to identify ectopy-triggering ganglionated plexus (ET-GP) in the left atrium with synchronized high-frequency stimulation (50 mA, 40 Hz, 80 ms, 15 trains) during sinus rhythm. ET-GP sites were ablated with radiofrequency lesions until they were nonfunctional. Triggered atrial tachycardias were also mapped and ablated. Patients were followed for 12 months with scheduled Holter monitoring and patient-activated ECG recordings. The primary end point was atrial arrhythmia lasting ≥30 seconds after a 90-day blanking period.

RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were recruited: 8 patients with AF despite durably isolated PVs and 15 undergoing a first procedure for persistent AF. On average, 85±15 sites were tested in patients with isolated PVs (2.5±0.9 previous AF ablations, 61±9 years, LVEF 58±5%, LAd 41±2 mm), identifying 11.8±3.8 ET-GPs. Four of the eight patients also had ablation of triggered atrial tachycardias. Of the 15 patients undergoing a first procedure for persistent AF (duration 2.8±1.1 years, continuous AF ≥6 months in 80%, 64±7 years, LAd 43±2 mm), 10 completed a full left atrial ET-GP map of 102±37 tested sites. identifying 14±4.5 ET-GP sites. After a mean follow-up of 12 months and cessation of antiarrhythmic agents, arrhythmia-free survival was 63% in patients with durably isolated veins and 60% in those undergoing a first procedure for persistent AF.

CONCLUSIONS: The Tau20-RETROmapping system can identify and guide ablation of high-frequency stimulation-provoked ectopy-triggering ganglionated plexus during sinus rhythm as potential non-PV drivers of AF. This feasibility study shows promising outcomes that need exploration in larger randomized controlled studies.

title: Outcomes of Catheter Ablation for Ventricular Arrhythmias Performed With ECMO Support: A 10-Year Institutional Experience.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Patients requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for cardiogenic shock or hemodynamic instability due to ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) represent an extremely high-risk but understudied population. We aimed to evaluate the intraprocedural stability, predictors of in-hospital mortality, and long-term outcomes in patients undergoing ECMO-supported VA ablation.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 57 patients undergoing 64 catheter ablations of VAs with ECMO support (2016-2025). Independent predictors of in-hospital mortality were identified using multivariable-adjusted logistic regression.

RESULTS: The median age of the patients was 62 years, and 70% had ischemic cardiomyopathy. At ECMO initiation, 40 patients (70%) presented with cardiogenic shock and 43 (75%) with electrical storm. ECMO provided robust stability; minimum mean arterial pressure was similar between ventricular and nonventricular tachycardia (55 versus 60 mm Hg; P=0.124). In-hospital mortality was 42% (24/57 [95% CI, 30%-55%]). Multivariable analysis identified age (odds ratio [OR], 1.18 per year [95% CI, 1.05-1.38]; P=0.004), ischemic cardiomyopathy (OR, 24.3 [95% CI, 2.3-700.57]; P=0.005), chronic kidney disease (OR, 9.76 [95% CI, 1.89-73.26]; P=0.006), and New York Heart Association class III or IV (OR, 12.72 [95% CI, 1.86-158.46]; P=0.008) as mortality predictors, whereas VA elimination was an independent protector against in-hospital death (OR, 0.12 [95% CI, 0.01-0.77]; P=0.025). In patients presenting with electrical storm (n=43), VA elimination (n=33) was associated with significantly lower in-hospital mortality than VA recurrence (n=10; 27% versus 80%; P=0.007). Among survivors (n=33), 3-year survival was 78.0%, with low rates of cardiac death (3%, 1/33) during follow-up (11 [3-38] months).

CONCLUSIONS: ECMO-supported VA ablation is feasible and provides procedural stability. Although survival is limited by baseline reserve, VA elimination is associated with improved in-hospital outcomes, serving as a bridge to recovery or clinical decision.

title: CACNA2D2 Regulates Mitochondrial Function to Attenuate Fibrosis and Atrial Fibrillation via the cGAS-STING Pathway.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is thought to be driven by atrial fibrosis. A previous study has identified the expression of calcium voltage-gated channel auxiliary subunit alpha2delta2 (CACNA2D2) is significantly downregulated in patients with AF, but its functional role remains unclear.

METHODS: We analyzed CACNA2D2 expression levels using public databases and clinical samples. Fibroblast-specific Cacna2d2 knockout and overexpression models were established to assess its role in atrial fibrosis through in vivo electrophysiological recordings, histopathologic analysis, in vitro mitochondrial function assays, and biochemical studies. We also evaluated the role of Cacna2d2 in doxorubicin/myocardial infarction-induced cardiac fibrosis and carbon tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis models.

RESULTS: We observed α2δ2 (encoded by CACNA2D2) expression was significantly reduced in patients with AF and Ang II (angiotensin II)-induced AF mouse models. Fibroblast-specific knockout of Cacna2d2 exacerbated Ang II-induced atrial fibrosis, increasing AF susceptibility and duration, whereas overexpression reversed these effects. In cardiac fibroblasts, Cacna2d2 overexpression blocked induction of ACTA2 (α-SMA) and COL1A1 (Col1). Mechanistically, Cacna2d2 localized to mitochondria when overexpressed in fibroblasts, blocked TGF-β (transforming growth factor-beta)-induced reactive oxygen species production and inhibit the leakage of mitochondrial DNA through the BAX/BAK channel, suppressing the activation of the cGAS-STING pathway. Notably, exogenous supplementation of Cacna2d2-overexpressing mitochondria significantly suppressed TGF-β-induced α-SMA and Col1 expression in fibroblasts. Cacna2d2 knockdown increased mortality and α-SMA expression, aggravating cardiac fibrosis in doxorubicin-treated mice, whereas its overexpression attenuated myocardial infarction-induced cardiac fibrosis and carbon tetrachloride-induced hepatic fibrosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrates that Cacna2d2 exerts antifibrotic effects by preserving mitochondrial function and preventing mitochondrial DNA-cGAS-STING pathway activation, identifying Cacna2d2 as a promising novel target for fibrotic diseases, including AF.

title: Cardiovascular Outcomes Following Smartwatch Irregular Rhythm Notification: Findings From the Apple Heart Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Smartwatch irregular rhythm notifications (IRNs) can identify atrial fibrillation. IRNs' association with broader cardiovascular outcomes is unclear. We evaluated whether receipt of an IRN in the AHS (Apple Heart Study) was associated with subsequent self-reported cardiovascular events.

METHODS: We performed a post hoc analysis of the AHS, a prospective trial in the United States. Participants were enrolled via an iPhone app from 2017 to 2018; those who completed the end-of-study survey were included. The exposure was IRN receipt. Outcomes were self-reported new heart failure, myocardial infarction, stroke/transient ischemic attack, pulmonary embolism, and a composite of these events (major adverse cardiovascular events). Multivariable-adjusted logistic regression models included age, sex, heart failure, hypertension, diabetes, prior stroke/transient ischemic attack/systemic embolism, and vascular disease.

RESULTS: Among 293 944 participants who completed follow-up, 929 (0.32% [95% CI, 0.30%-0.34%]) received an IRN. Participants with an IRN were older, more often male, and had a greater burden of cardiovascular risk factors. At the end-of-study survey, completed 5 to 14 months after enrollment, IRN receipt was associated with higher adjusted odds of self-reported heart failure (odds ratio, 5.43 [95% CI, 3.09-9.57]), stroke/transient ischemic attack (odds ratio, 3.51 [1.91-6.45]), pulmonary embolism (odds ratio, 4.43 [1.92-10.20]), and major adverse cardiovascular events (odds ratio, 4.01 [2.80-5.73]). Among participants with an IRN but without atrial fibrillation, IRN receipt remained associated with statistically significantly higher adjusted odds of self-reported heart failure and major adverse cardiovascular events.

CONCLUSIONS: Receipt of a smartwatch IRN was associated with higher odds of subsequent self-reported cardiovascular events beyond atrial fibrillation. These findings suggest that IRNs may identify individuals at elevated short-term cardiovascular risk.

title: Recent-Onset Atrial Fibrillation: What to Do for Maximum Impact a Matter of Time, Choices and Real-world Challenges.
summary:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The aim of this narrative review is to provide a practical and current perspective on how care for recent onset atrial fibrillation (AF) can be optimized, taking into account both the principles of AF care described in current guidelines and barriers in clinical practice. Within this framework, the latest evidence on anticoagulation, long-term rate versus rhythm control and comorbidities management is presented. Areas of clinical uncertainty are illustrated to help both cardiologists and emergency medicine physicians navigate new-onset AF.

RECENT FINDINGS: Early rhythm control can improve AF outcomes among recent onset AF patients, with catheter ablation emerging as a disease-modifying strategy, leading to improved long-term outcomes and a lower rate of arrhythmia recurrences compared with antiarrhythmic drugs. Early rhythm control, together with structured risk factors modification and oral anticoagulation can strongly influence the course of AF and are particularly effective in the early stages of AF. Patient education, starting from the Emergency Department is pivotal in shaping the future trajectory of AF patients.

title: Optimizing rate control in atrial fibrillation: conduction system pacing vs biventricular pacing
Outcomes of surgical ablation for atrial fibrillation in adults with congenital heart disease.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the outcomes of concomitant surgical ablation for atrial fibrillation in adults with congenital heart disease.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 42 patients (mean age, 58.5 ± 14.3 years) who underwent the maze procedure or pulmonary vein isolation concomitantly with intracardiac surgery between September 2003 and November 2022. None of the patients underwent surgery primarily for arrhythmia management.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients underwent the modified Cox maze procedure; two patients additionally underwent a combination of right atrial maze and pulmonary vein isolation, one patient underwent right atrial maze alone, and ten patients underwent pulmonary vein isolation alone. Over a mean follow-up of 39 ± 34.9 months, late mortality occurred in five patients, including two cardiac deaths. Recurrent atrial fibrillation was observed in 11 patients. Atrial fibrillation recurrence-free rates were 85.4%, 81.9%, and 75.6% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. During follow-up, one patient experienced an ischemic stroke, and three patients required implantation of a new pacemaker. Exploratory analysis suggested that advanced age at the time of surgery was associated with atrial fibrillation recurrence.

CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant surgical ablation for atrial fibrillation was suggested as a safe and effective treatment in adults with congenital heart disease. Earlier intervention, conducted before advanced age, may be associated with improved long-term rhythm outcomes.

title: Ventricular Septal Pulsed Field Ablation: Noninvasive, Longitudinal Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Lesion Structure and Function in a Preclinical Model.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an emerging myocardial ablation strategy, but lesion evolution and noninvasive assessment in ventricular myocardium remain incompletely characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate interventricular septal (IVS) PFA in a preclinical swine model and assess the feasibility of serial cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) for lesion characterization.

METHODS: Eight swine were allocated to acute and chronic cohorts. PFA was delivered to the IVS using a variable-loop circular catheter (VLCC). Multimodality assessments included electroanatomic mapping, serial CMR, echocardiography and pathology. Pathological lesion-depth measurements were obtained at terminal timepoints, whereas serial CMR enabled within-animal longitudinal assessment. CMR-pathology correspondence was evaluated using anatomically matched slices.

RESULTS: Serial CMR showed reductions in late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-derived lesion mass and volume by Day 21, with stabilization thereafter. Among 37 matched CMR-pathology slices from five animals, CMR-LGE-derived lesion-depth measurements showed positive association with pathology-derived measurements (Pearson's r = 0.77), moderate reliability (ICC = 0.74), and a mean difference of 0.03 mm, with 95% limits of agreement from -1.15 to 1.21 mm. Both methods showed decreased chronic lesion depths, consistent with lesion maturation and fibrotic remodeling. Transient reductions in left ventricular ejection fraction and regional septal mechanics were observed after PFA, followed by partial recovery.

CONCLUSION: Ventricular septal PFA produced well-demarcated lesions that evolved into chronic fibrotic scars. Serial CMR enabled noninvasive assessment of lesion localization, depth, and temporal evolution, with lesion-depth measurements showing correspondence with anatomically matched pathological measurements, supporting the feasibility of CMR for longitudinal assessment after ventricular PFA.

title: Successful Catheter Ablation of Premature Ventricular Contractions Originating from the Intermediate Accessory Papillary Muscle.
Arrhythmia-specific timing of first detection during extended textile ECG monitoring: a recording-level cumulative incidence analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Extended ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring improves detection of intermittent arrhythmias, but real-world recordings often have variable duration, and conventional diagnostic-yield curves may not account for censoring.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 9629 anonymized ambulatory ECG recordings of at least 24 h acquired in routine clinical practice between 2018 and 2024. Endpoints were first ECG-defined detection of atrial fibrillation (AF) burden ≤1% and ≤ 10%, non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (nsVT), pauses >3 s, bradycardia <40 beats/min for ≥60 s, and premature ventricular contraction (PVC) burden >10%. Arrhythmias were algorithm-flagged and staff-verified. Kaplan-Meier estimates were used to derive day-30-normalized cumulative incidence functions (CIF*).

RESULTS: Arrhythmias of interest were detected in 3611 recordings (37.5%). Median observed monitoring duration was 15.4 days (interquartile range 8.2-28.2). At day 14, CIF* was 65.8% for AF burden ≤1%, 71.0% for AF burden ≤10%, and 71.1% for nsVT, indicating continued first detections during days 14-30. In contrast, PVC burden >10% accumulated early, with CIF* of 59.6% at 24 h and 71.5% at 5 days.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large recording-level cohort, first ECG-defined detection timing differed by arrhythmia target. Low-burden AF and nsVT continued to accrue after day 14, whereas frequent PVC burden was usually identified earlier. These findings support target-specific monitoring strategies, while clinical actionability could not be assessed in this anonymized variable-duration dataset.

title: Reversal of Late Gadolinium Enhancement MRI-Assessed Left Atrial Fibrosis Following Cardioversion in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) cardioversion may reverse atrial remodeling.

PURPOSE: To investigate whether LGE-MRI-assessed left atrial (LA) fibrosis regresses after persistent atrial fibrillation (PersAF) cardioversion to sinus rhythm, and to analyze the relationship between fibrosis change and traditional volume-based measures of LA reverse remodeling.

STUDY TYPE: Prospective.

POPULATION: Fifty-three patients following cardioversion for PersAF.

FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3 T, cine balanced steady-state free precession cine and 3D inversion recovery gradient-echo sequences.

ASSESSMENT: MRI was performed 1-3 days after AF-cardioversion (early follow-up), and again at 3 months (late follow-up). Image analysis was performed by two observers using CVI42 and ADAS software. Data were compared between early and late follow-up. LA fibrosis on LGE-MRI was categorized by the image intensity ratio (IIR): core zone (IIR > 1.61) and border zone (0.97 < IIR ≤ 1.61). Maximum LA volume (LAVmax), LA ejection fraction (LAEF), LA strain, and left ventricular mass were assessed from cine data. An LAVmax reduction ≥ 15% from early to late follow-up defined LA reverse remodeling.

STATISTICAL TESTS: Early and late follow-up data were compared using paired t-tests. Multivariable analysis was performed to assess the associations between changes in LA border and core zone and other LA parameters. A p-value < 0.05 was considered significant.

RESULTS: Seventeen patients had volume-based LA reverse. Compared with early follow-up, LA border zone (22.2 [11.8-37.0] vs. 18.1 [11.8-25.2] cm2) and core zone (0.9 ± 3.0 vs. 0.1 ± 0.6 cm2) were significantly decreased. LAVmax was significantly reduced (97.2 ± 26.3 vs. 109.4 ± 32.7 mL), and LAEF (44.1 ± 15.8 vs. 32.2% ± 13.1%) and LA strain (27.4 ± 14.1 vs. 18.2% ± 8.6%) improved. Volume-based LA reverse remodeling was unrelated to ΔLA border (p = 0.955) or Δcore zone (p = 0.301).

DATA CONCLUSION: PersAF conversion to sinus rhythm resulted in a reduction in LGE-defined atrial enhancement, LAV reduction, and improved function. Fibrosis regression was independent of volume-based LA reverse remodeling.

EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2.

TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 4.

title: Experiences of Patients with Atrial Fibrillation Across the Continuum of Care: A Patient Journey Map Based on Qualitative Research.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Previous qualitative studies have described individual aspects of living with atrial fibrillation (AF), but patients' experiences across successive stages of the care journey remain insufficiently integrated.

METHODS: A qualitative descriptive design was used. Between March 2025 and December 2025, 20 patients with AF were purposively recruited from two tertiary hospitals in northern China and completed single-session retrospective semistructured interviews. Data were analyzed using inductive qualitative content analysis, and patient journey mapping was subsequently used as a secondary data-integration and visualization framework to organize findings along the clinical care timeline.

RESULTS: The AF journey comprised three stages and eight touchpoints: screening and diagnosis, treatment and intervention, and long-term management. Eleven themes were identified across three dimensions: tasks, emotions, and pain points. Screening and diagnosis were characterized by difficulties interpreting symptoms, fear of serious illness, and a fragmented pathway to diagnosis. Treatment and intervention involved complex risk-benefit decisions, treatment-related ambivalence, and difficulties translating clinical information into home self-management. Long-term management was characterized by medication and monitoring difficulties, persistent concerns about recurrence, fragmented follow-up, reduced engagement after symptom relief, and self-management fatigue.

CONCLUSION: Patients' experiences were stage-specific, with recurrent patterns evident across the AF care continuum. Emotional responses, risk perceptions, and self-management behaviors were intertwined with patients' experiences at different stages. Patient journey mapping may provide a potentially useful framework for identifying stage-specific needs and vulnerable transitions and may inform future efforts to strengthen patient-centered continuity of care.

title: Population Mortality Involving Co-Reported Intracerebral Hemorrhage and Atrial Fibrillation or Flutter in the United States, 1999-2025: Trends, Demographic Disparities, and Forecasts to 2040.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common indication for long-term oral anticoagulation, and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is the most feared bleeding complication of that treatment. National mortality data describing deaths in which both conditions are recorded remain limited. Temporal, demographic, and geographic trends in US population mortality involving co-reported ICH and AF or atrial flutter from 1999 to 2025, with projections to 2040, were examined.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of death certificate data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (CDC WONDER) database was conducted, identifying deaths listing ICH (International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision [ICD-10] code I61) and AF or atrial flutter (ICD-10 code I48) in any cause-of-death field. Records were extracted on June 15, 2026; data for 1999 through 2024 came from final Multiple Cause of Death files and data for 2025 from the provisional file. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were calculated per 100,000 total resident US population and stratified by sex, race/ethnicity, census region, and urbanization. Joinpoint regression assessed temporal trends, and autoregressive integrated moving average models projected rates through 2040.

RESULTS: From 1999 to 2025, 52,967 deaths with co-reported ICH and AF or atrial flutter were identified. The overall age-adjusted mortality rate rose from 0.4 to 0.7 per 100,000 between 1999 and 2021 (annual percent change [APC] 1.53%, p = 0.016) before stabilizing through 2025. Age-adjusted mortality rates were higher among men than among women in every study year and increased across the study period among Black or African American decedents (APC 1.83%, p < 0.000001). Rates were highest in the West, which recorded the highest or joint highest regional rate in every study year except 2018, and in nonmetropolitan areas, which equaled or exceeded metropolitan rates in every year from 2012 onward; the Northeast was the only region with a significant decline after 2015. Pooled state AAMRs ranged from 0.3 in Louisiana to 1.1 in Vermont, and 75.4% of deaths occurred in medical facilities.

CONCLUSIONS: Population mortality involving co-reported ICH and AF or atrial flutter rose until 2021 and then stabilized, with differences by sex, race and ethnicity, and geography that persisted across the study period. Age-adjusted rates are projected to remain broadly stable through 2040. These findings are descriptive. They do not establish that AF, anticoagulation, or anti-coagulation-associated bleeding caused the hemorrhages recorded, and differences in hypertension control and anticoagulation management remain plausible but untested explanations that warrant direct study.

title: Incidence, Risk Factors and Natural History of Atrial Arrhythmias in Patients With Systemic Right Ventricle.
summary:
BACKGROUND: The incidence and risk factors for atrial arrhythmia (AA; atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter) in adults with systemic right ventricle (sRV), specifically congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries and dextro-transposition of the great arteries palliated with atrial switch procedures, are not well understood. This study aims to better define these risks.

METHODS: Adults with sRV presenting to Mayo Clinic between 2000 and 2022 were identified. Their clinical characteristics, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic parameters at the time of first presentation were recorded. The incidence of sustained AA (>30 seconds) during follow-up was documented. Cox regression analysis was used to identify associations of incident atrial fibrillation/atrial flutter and mortality during follow-up.

RESULTS: Among 447 patients with sRV (median age, 33.1 [24.6-42.8], 55.9% male, 247 cm3-TGA; 200 dextro-transposition of the great arteries postatrial switch), AA was present at first visit in 113 (25.3%). Out of the remaining 334 patients, new-onset AA occurred in 125 (37.4%) patients during a median follow-up of 11.1 years (interquartile range, 3.6-19.3). Isolated atrial fibrillation was observed in 89 (37.4%), isolated atrial flutter in 76 (31.9%), and both atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter in 73 (30.7%) patients. In multivariable analysis, the risk factors for incident AA included age (hazard ratio, 1.04 [1.03-1.06]; P<0.001), d-TGA (hazard ratio, 1.96 [1.00-3.85]; P=0.05), and QRS duration (hazard ratio, 1.01 [1.00-1.02]; P=0.02). AA was associated with hospitalization for heart failure in 19% of patients. Among those treated with anti-arrhythmic drugs and ablation, recurrence occurred in over 50% of patients. AA was not an independent predictor of mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: AA occurred in more than half of this cohort with sRV, with risk increasing significantly after the third decade of life. Advancing age, dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and prolonged QRS duration were associated with increased risk of AA. Close monitoring for AA and early interventions are warranted in all adults with sRV.

title: Preferential Conduction Along the Epicardial Ventricular Septum During Idiopathic Ventricular Arrhythmias Originating From the Basal LV Summit: A Pitfall for Anatomical Ablation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: An anatomical ablation of idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) originating from the left ventricular summit (LVS) is delivered from endocardial sites across the myocardium adjacent to the site of the VA origin with the guidance of transvenous epicardial mapping. Therefore, electrophysiological information obtained by transvenous epicardial mapping should be carefully interpreted.

OBJECTIVES: This study investigated ventricular activation patterns within the great cardiac vein (GCV) during idiopathic LVS VAs.

METHODS: We studied 38 consecutive patients who underwent a successful endocardial ablation of idiopathic LVS VAs at the left ostial process, left coronary sinus, and commissure between the left and right coronary cusps.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients exhibited a radial activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded around the junction between the GCV and anterior interventricular vein (AIVV). The remaining 9 patients exhibited a septal activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded within the AIVV, with the activation sequence being from the AIVV to GCV. The septal group mainly exhibited left bundle branch block pattern, whereas the radial group exhibited right bundle branch block pattern (P < 0.0001). The distance between the earliest ventricular activation site within the GCV or AIVV and the successful ablation site was significantly larger for LVS VAs with a septal activation pattern than those with a radial activation pattern.

CONCLUSIONS: During idiopathic basal LVS VAs, activation from those VA origins often preferentially conducted along the ventricular septum. It should be kept in mind that this unusual activation pattern may mislead the mapping and catheter ablation of LVS VAs.

title: Discontinuation of Anticoagulation in Patients at Relatively High Risk of Stroke After Successful Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulant (OAC) discontinuation after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation may be feasible in selected patients; however, outcomes in those at high stroke risk remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate associations between OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after ablation and thromboembolic or bleeding events across CHA2DS2-VA risk strata.

METHODS: Patients without AF recurrence within 12 months of catheter ablation and with CHA2DS2-VA scores ≥2 were identified from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database and classified as OAC continuers or discontinuers based on prescription coverage at the 12-month landmark. The primary outcome was a composite of stroke or systemic embolism and major bleeding. Doubly robust estimation combined overlap weighting with covariate-adjusted Cox regression, stratified by CHA2DS2-VA score (2-4 and ≥5).

RESULTS: Among 3,637 patients (mean age: 60.8 ± 9.7 years, 27.1% female, mean CHA2DS2-VA 3.2 ± 1.3), discontinuation in those with scores of 2-4 (n = 3,054) was associated with lower risks of the composite event (HR: 0.61; 95% CI: 0.38-0.96) and major bleeding (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.29-0.90), without increased stroke or systemic embolism (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.34-1.58). In those with scores ≥5 (n = 583), discontinuation was not significantly associated with any outcome, and tests for interaction were not significant (all P > 0.46).

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after AF ablation was associated with decreased bleeding risk without a corresponding increase in thromboembolic events among patients with CHA2DS2-VA score 2 to 4.

title: Electrical storm due to ectopic activity following successful reperfusion: Clinical characterization and pharmacological approach to angry Purkinje syndrome
summary: Introduction: Angry Purkinje syndrome is an uncommon cause of electrical storm characterized by short-coupled premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) originating from the His-Purkinje system and triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PMVT) or ventricular fibrillation (VF). It may occur during the subacute phase after myocardial infarction despite successful coronary reperfusion and absence of recurrent ischemia. Case presentation: A 55-year-old man presented with persistent oppressive precordial chest pain, rated 8/10, radiating to the jaw and left arm, which had begun at 02:00 h while asleep, without associated autonomic symptoms. On admission, blood pressure was 174/101 mmHg and heart rate was 103 beats/min. Electrocardiography showed an extensive anterior myocardial infarction, and primary percutaneous coronary intervention restored TIMI 3 flow in the left anterior descending coronary artery. Seventy-two hours after complete coronary revascularization, the patient developed ventricular fibrillation requiring external defibrillation with 150 J (Figure 2E). At the time of the first arrest, serum troponin was 896 pg/mL, potassium was 4.5 mEq/L, and magnesium was 2.62 mEq/L. The heart rate was 50 beats/min, with a QTc of 413 ms. Continuous cardiac monitoring subsequently demonstrated frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) with a coupling interval of approximately 380 ms and a right bundle branch block morphology with a superior axis, followed by episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PMVT) initiated by short-coupled PVCs (Figure 2A–D). Following this event, diagnostic coronary angiography was performed because of suspected acute stent thrombosis, confirming patency of the left anterior descending coronary artery stent with TIMI 3 flow and no new angiographic lesions in the remaining coronary arteries. Conclusion: Angry Purkinje syndrome should be considered in patients who develop recurrent PMVT or VF initiated by short-coupled PVCs after successful myocardial reperfusion, particularly when recurrent ischemia has been excluded. Flecainide combined with atrial overdrive pacing may represent a potential rescue strategy when quinidine is unavailable; however, further evidence is required to determine its efficacy and safety in this setting.

title: Unexpected Non-immune Hydrops Foetalis With Supraventricular Tachycardia in a Premature Neonate
Implantable Cardiac Monitor for Diagnosis and Continuous Monitoring of Type 1 Brugada Electrocardiographic Pattern.
summary:
BACKGROUND: The spontaneous type 1 Brugada electrocardiographic pattern (BrECG) is a recognized marker of increased arrhythmic risk in Brugada syndrome (BrS), but its dynamic nature may limit detection with conventional electrocardiographic monitoring.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of implantable cardiac monitors (ICMs) with remote monitoring for detecting spontaneous BrECG in asymptomatic patients.

METHODS: Consecutive patients showing ajmaline-induced BrECG were prospectively enrolled. During drug challenge, surface potential mapping was performed to identify the optimal implantation position, after which a long-sensing vector ICM was inserted subcutaneously. The primary endpoint was the time to first documentation of spontaneous BrECG based on recordings remotely transmitted by the implanted ICM during follow-up.

RESULTS: Fifty-nine patients (46±15 years, 69% male) underwent ICM implantation without complications. The left upper thoracic region with negative inclination was identified as the optimal position for BrECG detection. During a median follow-up of 21.6 months, BrECG was documented in 29 patients (49%); 72% were diagnosed within one month and 86% within two months after implantation. Family history of BrS (p=0.050) and longer QRS duration (p=0.032) were independently associated with diagnosis, whereas higher ajmaline dose was inversely associated (p=0.006). Among 50,666 transmitted recordings, 3.4% showed a positive BrECG, increasing to 7.4% during nighttime, and with a trend toward a higher probability of detection at lower mean daily heart rates.

CONCLUSION: Continuous ICM monitoring using a long-sensing vector in the left upper thoracic region with negative inclination enables detection of spontaneous BrECG and reveals substantial temporal variability of the ECG phenotype in patients with drug-induced BrECG.

title: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation in children and young adults with severe adrenergically mediated ventricular arrhythmias: a single-centre experience.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: Left cardiac sympathetic denervation is established for selected high-risk inherited arrhythmia syndromes, but evidence for an intended bilateral strategy in children and young adults remains limited. We evaluated the rationale, feasibility, safety, follow-up ascertainment, and outcomes of intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation.

METHODS: Consecutive children and young adults undergoing intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation between January 2015 and November 2025 were reviewed. The operation targeted the lower stellate component and upper thoracic sympathetic chain bilaterally, usually through single-port thoracoscopic access. Outcomes were obtained from specialist cardiology follow-up, electrocardiography, Holter monitoring, exercise testing when available, inpatient telemetry, device interrogation, and medication records.

RESULTS: Thirty-seven patients were operated. Mean age was 12.4 years. Bilateral denervation was completed in 36 patients; 1 underwent left-sided denervation only owing to intraoperative haemodynamic instability. Single-port access was used in 30 patients. There were no intraoperative deaths, unplanned full thoracotomy conversions, intercostal injuries, reoperations for surgical complications, or denervation-related permanent pacing. Procedure-attributable morbidity comprised one mild Horner syndrome and one self-limited axillary wound complaint. Among 36 patients with post-discharge follow-up, 32 remained free from the primary malignant ventricular arrhythmic endpoint. Estimated malignant ventricular arrhythmia-free survival was 95.8 per cent at 1 year and 89.4 per cent at 3 years.

CONCLUSION: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation was feasible and had low procedure-attributable morbidity in selected young patients. It should be interpreted as an adjunct to multidisciplinary arrhythmia care, not as a replacement for medication, device surveillance, or follow-up.

title: Sex Disparities in Outcomes and Safety of Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation With Percutaneous Mechanical Circulatory Support.
Perioperative Decision-Making in a Complex Cardiac Patient Undergoing Pacemaker Lead Extraction and Minimally Invasive Tricuspid Valve Replacement.
Femoral sheath fracture and migration during temporary pacemaker removal: Successful bail-out using a balloon retrieval technique.
Predicting Major Adverse Events With Cardiac Resynchronization, Leadless, and Conduction System Pacemaker Implantation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Large-scale contemporary risk prediction models for adverse events after pacemaker implantation are lacking. The National Cardiovascular Data Registry EP Device Implant Registry has collected data on pacemaker implantations including cardiac resynchronization therapy pacemakers (CRT-P), leadless pacemakers, and His/left bundle pacemakers since April 2021.

OBJECTIVES: To produce a standardized risk model for in-hospital complications following CRT-P, leadless, and His/left bundle pacemaker procedures.

METHODS: Data from 21,211 novel pacemaker procedures across 179 hospitals from January 2022 to June 2024 were used to develop and validate a model to predict in-hospital complications.

RESULTS: The overall in-hospital complication rate was 2.00% (range 1.69%-2.23% and interquartile range 1.98%-2.01%), which varied somewhat by device type: CRT-P 1.76%, leadless pacemaker 2.51%, and His/left bundle pacemaker 1.85%, p = 0.0052. Prior MI, prior cardiac arrest, sodium >145 mEq/L, and being hospitalized for cardiac or non-cardiac reasons not related to the procedure were the most significant risk factors for complications. The model demonstrated moderate discrimination with a C-index of 0.714 for the total cohort; this varied somewhat but showed helpful discrimination for each device-type (C-index of 0.716 for CRT-P, 0.795 for leadless pacemakers, and 0.663 for His/left bundle pacemakers).

CONCLUSIONS: We developed a risk model for CRT-P, leadless, and conduction system pacemakers with overall helpful risk prediction, although it varied by device type. Modifications to the EPDI Registry data collection form and larger numbers of procedures in the registry over time will allow for separate, device-specific risk models in the future that may offer improved performance.

title: Variability and Drivers of Battery Longevity in Contemporary Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Systems Across Geographic Regions.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Battery longevity of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) and cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillators (CRT-Ds) affects clinical outcomes and resource use, yet the contribution of regional practice patterns to battery consumption remains poorly characterized.

OBJECTIVES: We compared projected battery longevity of contemporary ICD and CRT-D systems across Asia-Pacific, Europe, and North America and evaluated factors associated with regional differences.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 138,897 transvenous ICD/CRT-D devices (market release 2019) from 36 countries in the global BIOTRONIK Home Monitoring database. Longevity was estimated using a validated linear battery-drain projection model. Devices were grouped by type and geographic region.

RESULTS: Median (Q1-Q3) longevity was highest for single-chamber ICD (14.8 [Q1-Q3: 14.0-15.5] years) and lowest for CRT-D (9.3 [Q1-Q3: 7.9-10.5] years). Longevity was longer in Asia-Pacific and Europe than in North America, with the longest estimates observed in Asia-Pacific subregional clusters and regional differences up to 2.0 years. High-voltage consumption showed limited regional variation. Larger differences were observed for low-voltage consumption and atrial pacing burden (8.7%-40.1%). Remote monitoring contributed <1% to battery drain, whereas telemetry-related energy consumption for in-office visits exhibited the greatest regional variability. Multivariable analyses identified pacing burden, follow-up intensity, and delivered shocks as independent correlates of projected battery longevity. Adjustment for these factors attenuated, but did not eliminate, regional differences.

CONCLUSIONS: Battery longevity of contemporary ICD/CRT-D systems varies substantially across geographic regions despite identical device technology, and may be potentially extended by attention to pacing-related device use and follow-up methods.

title: Cardioneuroablation for Vasovagal Syncope: A Systematic Computed Tomography-Guided Anatomical Approach.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Cardioneuroablation (CNA) targeting parasympathetic ganglionated plexi (GP) is a emerging therapy for vasovagal syncope (VVS). Various methods have been proposed to identify GPs and optimize acute denervation.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the results of an anatomy-guided, reproducible approach for CNA in patients with implantable loop recorder (ILR) and Holter based indication for ablation.

METHODS: Consecutive patients with VVS who underwent anatomy-guided CNA using segmented Computed Tomography (CT) imaging for ILR-guided indication were retrospectively included. The primary outcome included clinical recurrence of ILR-documented bradyarrhythmia.

RESULTS: Fifty-four patients (mean age 39.9±12.7, 50% female) from four centers were included. All patients had spontaneous cardioinhibitory syncope documented, predominantly by ILR (89%), with a mean pause duration of 17.5±12.6 seconds. Contrast-enhanced CT with epicardial fat segmentation identified GP locations and guided ablation in all patients. Extra-cardiac vagal stimulation (ECVS) was used as a procedural endpoint in 61.1% of patients. The superior paraseptal GP and the inferior paraseptal GP were the primary GPs targeted (90.7% and 96.3% respectively). Additional GPs were targeted when ECVS continued to induce sinus arrest or atrioventricular block after initial denervation. Mean procedural time was 127.5 ± 32 minutes. During a follow-up of 17.4±11.9 months, all patients were monitored with ILR; 9 patients (18%) experienced the primary outcome, including atrioventricular block in 33.3%.

CONCLUSION: An anatomically guided CNA strategy based on fat-pad segmented CT, combined with patient selection using documented spontaneous VVS events and follow-up with ILR, appears to be a practical approach for the management of VVS.

title: Global reporting of Brugada syndrome in VigiBase®: A disproportionality analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Brugada syndrome (BrS) represents a rare but potentially malignant cardiac channelopathy, which may be precipitated by drugs, although data mainly derive from case reports/series.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the global reporting of BrS with drugs, including co-occurrence patterns, and identify novel potential associations.

METHODS: We used VigiBase® to perform descriptive and disproportionality analyses. The reporting odds ratio (ROR) and Bayesian information component (IC) with relevant 95% confidence/credibility intervals (95% CI) were used as disproportionality measures to identify signals of disproportionate reporting (SDR). We performed a network analysis to assess the co-occurrence patterns of related medications based on Jaccard similarity.

RESULTS: We included 544 deduplicated cases of BrS (94.7% serious events, 30.9% females, median time to onset of 30 days, 40.8% physician-reported, 63% from North America), with bupropion (n = 50), nortriptyline (n = 40) and flecainide (n = 34) as most frequently reported suspected drugs. Among 39 drugs with at least four reports, 32 emerged with an SDR, of which 17 were not listed in the BrS website (http://www.brugadadrugs.org), such as clozapine and loperamide (often overdosed). The co-occurrence network included 17 medications, regardless of the labelled role (suspected, interacting or concomitant), with a total of 12 potential co-occurrences; fentanyl exhibited the highest closeness centrality (1.0), whereas the strongest co-occurrence was reported between bupropion and nortriptyline (Jaccard similarity of 0.31).

CONCLUSIONS: Notwithstanding limitations related to pharmacovigilance and the complex BrS pathophysiology, we identified 32 medications with over-reporting of BrS, including 17 drugs not listed in the BrS website as well as clusters in affective disorders and anaesthesia.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential and progression of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is associated with incident atrial fibrillation (AF). However, its relationship with AF progression remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To assess whether CHIP is associated with AF progression.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled patients with paroxysmal AF who underwent deep targeted sequencing for CHIP mutations between April 2021 and December 2022. Variant allele fraction (VAF) ≥2.0% defined CHIP. The primary endpoint was documented AF progression, defined as either (1) AF documented on at least two separate 12-lead ECGs obtained >1 week apart, or (2) 100% AF burden on extended ECG monitoring. We assessed the association between CHIP and AF progression using Cox proportional hazards regression. In patients with available left atrial (LA) electroanatomical mapping, we compared low-voltage areas (LVA) by clonal hematopoiesis (CH) status (VAF ≥1.0% cutoff).

RESULTS: Among the 310 patients (mean age 65.7±5.7 years), CHIP was present in 64 patients (20.6%). Over a mean follow-up of 2.6±1.0 years, documented AF progression occurred in 10/64 (15.6%) patients with CHIP and 15/246 (6.1%) without CHIP. CHIP was independently associated with AF progression [adjusted hazard ratio 3.38, 95% CI 1.45-7.85; P = 0.005]. In an exploratory mapping subgroup, extensive LVA (≥10.0%) was more frequent in CH [24.4% vs 9.5%; unadjusted OR 3.10, 95% CI 1.10-8.71] and numerically higher at the VAF ≥2.0% cutoff.

CONCLUSION: In patients with paroxysmal AF, CHIP was associated with a 3.4-fold higher risk of documented AF progression. Exploratory mapping findings suggest a possible association between CH and advanced atrial substrate, warranting further validation.

title: MiR-182 regulates IL-6 and HCN4 in the cardiac context: implications for human atrial electrical remodelling.
summary:
BACKGROUND: The progression of cardiac electrical remodelling and the onset of proarrhythmic events are multifactorial processes, with many factors contributing to atrial electrical remodelling and the consequent development of atrial fibrillation (AF). Recently, miR-182 has been identified as causative factors of arrhythmogenesis in animal models but its potential relationship with proinflammatory mediators such as interleukin-6 (IL-6), emerged as new key player in independent preclinical evidence for atrial electrogenesis, remains unknown.

METHODS: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) were differentiated into cardiomyocytes (CMs) to study the role of miR-182-overexpression (OE) in human cardiac background. Functional consequences were assessed by measuring spontaneous electrical activity by using MULTIPLE-High-Throughput and Intracell systems, with/without autonomic stimulation. Molecular analyses by RT-PCR/Elisa assays were performed. Hearts from the Tg(myl7:GAL4,EGFP)xTg(Sce.4xUAS: miR-182,cry: EGFP) zebrafish line [Tg(myl7 > miR-182)] were used to measure the expression of dre-il6. Human IL-6 protein (5,4 pg/nL) was microinjected in the pericardial region of 2dpf Tg(myl7:EGFP) wt-like zebrafish embryos and heart rate was recorded. Expression analyses were performed on human left atrial samples of 49 patients (11 controls, CT; 18 left atrial dilation (LA-D); 20 permanent AF).

RESULTS: MiR-182-OE in hiPS-CMs significantly impact cardiac electrophysiology showing reduced and irregular spontaneous beating rate. Accordingly, MiR-182-OE downregulated the expression of HCN4, encoding for the pacemaker f-current, incrementing IL-6 expression and secretion and via ISL1. On the contrary, 24-48 h incubation with IL-6 (50ng/mL) did not change miR-182-5p expression levels in CT hiPS-CMs. The IL-6 receptor antagonist tocilizumab (TOC, 10 µg/mL) partially rescued HCN4 expression in miR-182-OE hiPS-CMs. Interestingly, miR-182-OE in hiPS-CMs enhanced response to acetylcholine and dysregulated genes associated with atrial pathology. Zebrafish heart samples from Tg(myl7 > miR-182) exhibited increased il6 expression levels. Pericardial injection of human IL-6 in wt zebrafish embryos decreased heart rate. Finally, miR-182-5p was found to be overexpressed in human biopsies from patients with LA-D, with the highest expression levels observed in patients with permanent AF; remarkably, miR-182 levels were positively correlated with IL-6 expression.

CONCLUSION: The results support the hypothesis of a causative link between miR-182-OE and IL-6 production in the cardiac context. This molecular axis may represent an associated molecular signature predisposing to arrhythmogenesis. Overall, our findings reveal novel pathophysiological mechanisms concordant across models and suggest novel pharmacological targets within the complex AF setting.

title: Right Ventricular Cardiomyocyte Dysfunction and Arrhythmogenesis in a Bleomycin-induced Mouse Model of Group 3 Pulmonary Hypertension.
summary: Group 3 pulmonary hypertension (PH) occurs when lung diseases induce hypoxic vasoconstriction and pulmonary vascular remodeling. The increase in pulmonary vascular resistance elevates right ventricular (RV) afterload leading to progressive ventricular dysfunction. The mechanisms underlying cardiomyocyte dysfunction in Group 3 PH remain poorly characterized, despite RV pathology representing a critical component of disease progression. Using a mouse model of intratracheal bleomycin-induced PH, we tested the hypothesis that RV function and cardiomyocyte excitation-contraction coupling (ECC) are impaired in PH. Male and female mice were administered intratracheal saline (Sham) or bleomycin to induce PH and assess for sex differences across cardiac parameters. Langendorff-perfused working heart preparations revealed that PH mice display greater RV pressure development, elevated end diastolic pressure, and more spontaneous ventricular arrhythmias versus Sham. Structurally, hearts of PH mice exhibited increased RV hypertrophy and fibrosis versus Sham, with the hypertrophic response more pronounced in males versus females. To assess Ca2+ dynamics and cellular contractile function, enzymatically isolated cardiomyocytes were subjected to electrical field stimulation (0.5-4 Hz, fura-2 dye). RV cardiomyocyte ECC was impaired in PH versus Sham mice, including elevated diastolic Ca2+ and shorter diastolic sarcomere lengths, depressed Ca2+ transient and sarcomere contraction amplitudes, and slower Ca2+ decay rates with slower sarcomere relaxation. Left ventricular (LV) cardiomyocytes did not display these changes. Taken together, these data indicate impairment in RV ECC in the bleomycin-induced PH model, highlighting multiple Ca2+ handling abnormalities that may contribute to the RV dysfunction and arrhythmogenesis observed clinically in PH.
journal: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

title: Genetic variants of transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy associated with low sensitivity to bone scintigraphy: a systematic review.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA) is characterized by amyloid deposition and frequently leads to a progressive cardiomyopathy with poor prognosis. Bone scintigraphy with 99mTc-labeled tracers is the cornerstone of noninvasive diagnosis, yet several hereditary TTR variants are associated with false-negative or low-grade tracer uptake.

OBJECTIVES: To identify all TTR variants associated with false-negative bone scintigraphy in hereditary ATTR-CA and discuss clinical implications.

METHODS: Medline, Scopus, and Cochrane were searched from inception to July 2025 per PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies included observational studies, case series, and case reports of patients with confirmed ATTR-CA undergoing TTR genetic testing and 99mTc scintigraphy.

RESULTS: Nineteen studies (108 patients) met inclusion criteria. Thirteen pathogenic TTR variants were associated with low or absent uptake (Perugini grade 0-1); p.Val50Met, p.Phe84Leu, and p.Ser97Tyr were most consistently implicated, while p.Val142Ile showed false-negative results in ∼5-10% of carriers. In 11 of 13 variants, advanced structural cardiomyopathy was confirmed despite negative scintigraphy.

CONCLUSIONS: Bone scintigraphy has important limitations in specific hereditary TTR variants. A negative scan does not exclude cardiac involvement in genetically at-risk patients. Multimodal strategies including CMR and histological assessment are essential for timely diagnosis.

title: ecg-coding-agents: local and commercial coding agents computing QT, QTc, and HRV from PhysioNet ECG recordings
summary: Harness, task set, expert-derived references, scoring, and aggregate results for a preregistered evaluation of language-model coding agents that write and run Python to measure QT, corrected QT, and frequency-domain heart-rate variability from PhysioNet recordings (QT Database, Fantasia, MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database). Three locally run open-weight models (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) and one commercial model (DeepSeek-V4-flash) run 99 tasks five times each, with the agent's code executed in a network-free container; a library-only NeuroKit2 pipeline is the baseline, and an exploratory arm appends a reference of the installed library functions to the system prompt of the local models. Version 1.1.0 adds the post hoc checks (constant-answer and RR-model baselines, run-level QT agreement, provenance of answered numbers) and a preregistered confirmatory QT test on 31 held-out QT Database records (155 runs), with its plan, scripts, outputs, and transcripts. No PhysioNet data are included.
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
